headline: Gold Lounge gets one-week suspension, $500 fine, and closing hours rolled back to 11:30 until December 31
summary: The one-week suspension starts on the 17th, and the business has five business days to appeal it to the ABCC. A police captain said officers were called to the club on October 4th, 2026, after a young woman said she was beaten up and her phone was taken. Officers said minors were drinking inside, and the owner gave a different account. Four other license requests were approved, and Mamasita received a written warning.
decisions: Approved transfer of the Envy Lounge liquor license to Rumba Bar.
Approved change of manager, officers, insurance, and DBA name for Attika Restaurant at 1 Miller Street.
Approved a one-week suspension of Gold Lounge's license, starting on the 17th, a $500 fine, and rolling back closing hours to 11:30 until December 31st.
Approved a common victualler license at 261-265 Broadway.
Approved a one-day alcohol license for Limonenses Unidos en el Exterior event on the 29th.
Approved a written warning for Mamasita over underage drinking.
discussion: Gold Lounge suspension: A two-week suspension and hours rollback were first proposed, then changed to one week, a $500 fine, and 11:30 closing until December 31. The club's owner said he had hired more security and that this was his first such incident.

October 4th incident: Police said a young woman reported being beaten up and having her phone taken, and that minors were drinking inside a club with its front door locked. The owner said a fight between two women started outside the club and that he had asked everyone to leave.

Mamasita incident: Police said a man who entered on an ID showing he was over 21 later gave officers one showing he was under 21. The security company's owner said the company now uses UV lights to check IDs.
Door and security rules: Members said locked doors and security staff needed attention, including a person posted outside when doors are closed and no handcuffs for security staff.
